title: Best E-signature software
content_html:
The best e-signature software is the one that fits how your documents already move: who signs, how often, and where the signed file has to end up. For many teams a well-known standalone signing service such as DocuSign or Adobe Acrobat Sign is enough. When signing is one step inside a longer process, a tool built into that process often fits better.

What is it

E-signature software lets people sign documents on a screen instead of on paper. You upload or create a document, send it to the people who need to sign, and get back a signed copy. Most tools also show who has signed and who has not.

It matters because unsigned documents hold up work. A contract that sits in someone's inbox delays the next step. A signed copy saved in the wrong folder is hard to find later.

The main options

There are several types of e-signature tools. Each one suits a different kind of team.

OptionExamplesWho it suits
Standalone e-signature servicesDocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign, Dropbox SignTeams that sign contracts now and then and want something ready to use today
Dutch e-signature servicesSignhost, ValidSignTeams that prefer a supplier based in the Netherlands
Signing built into off-the-shelf software packagesThe signing feature in a document, CRM or accounting package you already pay forTeams whose documents already start in that package
Low-code platformsMendix, OutSystemsTeams with their own developers who want to build a signing step into an internal app
Custom softwareDutch custom software agencies, your in-house IT teamTeams where signing is one step in a longer process that no package fits

DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign and Dropbox Sign are the simplest place to start. They are widely used, so your signers may already know how they work, and you can begin without a project. Acrobat Sign is a natural choice if your team already works in Adobe Acrobat.

Signhost and ValidSign are Dutch e-signature services. They suit teams that would rather deal with a supplier in the Netherlands.

Built-in signing in off-the-shelf software packages saves you from adding one more tool. Check whether it covers everything you need before you buy something separate.

Mendix and OutSystems are established low-code platforms. They let your own developers build internal apps faster, and a signing step can be part of such an app. They work best when you already have people who can build and maintain those apps.

Custom software, built by a Dutch custom software agency or your in-house IT team, only makes sense when the signing step is tied to other work. Examples are a contract that has to update your CRM, or a form that has to go into your ERP. An in-house IT team already knows your systems, which is a real advantage. For most teams custom software is more than they need.

How to choose the best e-signature software

Start with your process, not with a feature list. These questions narrow the choice quickly.

  • Who signs? Internal staff, customers, suppliers, or all three. External signers need a process that is easy to follow without an account.
  • How often? A few contracts a month is a different need than a constant flow of forms.
  • Where do documents come from? If they start in your CRM or ERP, look at how the signing tool connects to it. A good connection means data is entered once instead of typed over.
  • Where does the signed file go? Decide in advance where signed copies are stored and who can find them.
  • What do the rules require? Requirements can differ by country and by type of document. Ask a legal adviser which kind of signature your documents need.
  • Where is the data stored? Read the vendor's terms and processing agreement to see where documents are kept and who can access them.
  • How are you charged? Compare the licence model with how many people will actually send documents.

Signing is often only half the job. The document also has to reach the other party safely. Email attachments and shared links are not always the safest way to send sensitive files, so consider that step too.

FAQ

What is the best e-signature software?

The best e-signature software is the one that matches who signs, how often, and where signed files need to go. For occasional contracts, a standalone service such as DocuSign or Adobe Acrobat Sign, or the signing feature in your existing software, is usually enough. When signing is part of a longer process, a tool built into that process can fit better.

Is the signing feature in my existing software good enough?

Often it is. Check whether it handles external signers, stores signed copies where you need them, and meets the requirements for your documents. If it does, you may not need a separate tool.

Are electronic signatures legally valid?

Rules can differ by country and by type of document. Ask a legal adviser which kind of signature your documents need before you pick a tool.

Where are my documents stored when I use e-signature software?

That depends on the vendor. Read its terms and processing agreement to see where documents are kept and who can access them.

Does Upward Technologies offer e-signature software?

Yes. DocSign is Upward Technologies' e-signature product.

When does custom e-signature software make sense?

It makes sense when signing is tied to other steps, such as updating a CRM or feeding an ERP, and no package fits that process. Low-code platforms like Mendix or OutSystems, a custom software agency or your in-house IT team can all build that kind of step. For simple contract signing, a ready-made tool is usually the better choice.
